I've been farming these six mu in Quzhou for over forty years, and my father farmed them before me. I know this land like I know my own hands. The soil here on the North China Plain is good black earth, but it needs care. I don't try anything fancy — I stick with what works, what the weather and the market have always rewarded around here.

**What I will grow and why:**

I will plant **winter wheat** this autumn and follow it with **summer maize** after the harvest, just like I always do. This double-crop rotation is the backbone of our county. The wheat gives me a stable income because the grain station buys it at a guaranteed price, and the maize earns good money from the feed mills and traders who come right to the village. I thought about growing vegetables once, but the price swings are too risky at my age, and my back isn't what it used to be. Grain is safe. I need safe.

For the wheat, I will use an **improved variety** — the seed dealer at the cooperative has one that resists lodging and does well with our water. For maize, I will buy **hybrid seed**; everyone uses hybrids now because the yield difference is too big to ignore. I will till with the **rotary tiller** before wheat planting to break up the stubble and level the field. After the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant maize with **no-tillage** direct seeding into the wheat stubble — there's no time to waste between crops, and the stubble mulch keeps some moisture in.

**How I will manage them:**

I will fertilize based on what the soil needs and what I can afford. For wheat, I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress with urea at green-up and jointing. For maize, I will apply basal fertilizer and side-dress at the big-flare stage. I will irrigate the wheat three times — overwinter, at jointing, and at grain filling — because spring drought is our biggest enemy. The maize will get one good irrigation at flowering if the summer turns dry, maybe two if it's a bad year. I'll spray pesticides two or three times on the wheat for aphids and rust, and once or twice on the maize for borers. I don't spray for every little thing — I watch the fields and decide.

I expect about 500 kg per mu of wheat and 550 kg per mu of maize if the weather cooperates. That should give me enough to sell and keep some for household grain.
